question: At exp04's window (after the start line, layers 36-50), does a linear code for the intermediate colour, fit on other items, make the model take X as the step (answer f(X)) where the lens direction v_X - v_I does not? Does reshaping the lens direction by the activation covariance (Σv) do it?
why: Chosen by the human (Zach, 2026-10-15) after exp04's fresh replication and exp06: which direction carries brew's step at exp04's window. Design approved by the human before the run.

fit.gate: the model's greedy answer is A (exp03's reading)
fit.model: per window layer and position after the start line, ridge least squares (ridge 1.0, intercept not penalised) of the block output on one-hot codes of S, I and A over the 12-colour palette
fit.code: E_I[k], the coefficient row of intermediate colour k (each one-hot block's rows sum to zero)

sigma: the WikiText-103 test covariance of block outputs at the window layers, estimated as exp06's (100,000 positions, 512-token windows, position 0 left out)
eligibility: as exp04 (B answers A, C answers c, O answers A; C and O token-aligned with B), with the same tokens after the start line as the fit items

edits.copy: δ = h_C - h_B (exp04's copy), at the copy dose by definition
edits.random: a seeded Gaussian direction per position
edits.lens: v_X - v_I (unit lens vectors of the colours' concept tokens), the same at every position
edits.sigma_\u03bb: Σ_λ (v_X - v_I), Σ_λ = (1 - λ) Σ + λ (tr Σ / d) I, λ in [0.5, 0.0]
edits.code_jspace: the copy-dosed code's 25-atom signed OMP approximation over the lens's unit vectors of letter-bearing tokens

dose.copy: primary: each edit as large as the copy δ at that layer (total norm over the positions after the start line). code is rescaled by one factor, keeping its own spread over the positions; lens, sigma_λ and random take δ's norm at each position; code_jspace and code_rest are parts of the rescaled code
dose.code: code at its own size; random at the code's norm at each position

layers: each window layer on its own
outcome: the edited continuation's first palette colour as a role (b = f(X), X, I, A, ...), as exp04

decision.step_score: per item, the share of window layers at which the edit gives f(X); differences are paired bootstraps over items (95%)
decision.gate: the run is interpreted only if, on the fresh items, copy's step score exceeds random's (copy dose)
decision.code: primary, fresh items, copy dose: the code writes the step if code - random is above 0; it writes where the lens direction does not if code - lens (J++) is above 0 as well
decision.sigma: secondary: Σ-shaping helps if sigma_λ - lens is above 0 for λ = 0.5 or 0 (J++; the J-lens alike)
decision.code_parts: secondary, exp04's rule with random as the null: the code's step is outside the J-space if code_rest - code_jspace is above 0 and code_jspace - random is not; inside if code_jspace - code_rest is above 0 and code_rest - random is not; otherwise both or neither
decision.code_own_size: secondary: the code at its own size writes the step if code - random (code dose) is above 0
decision.replication: the same comparisons on the bank items, reported
decision.reproduce: copy must reproduce exp04's full-copy rows (parts_window_fresh, parts_window) item for item (reported)

diagnostics: read: on each test item's own activations, the intermediate decoded from the fit (given S and A), per layer; chance 1/12
the median cosine of the code to the lens direction and to each Σ_λ lens direction
the share of the code's squared norm in its J-space part, and of a random direction's (chance)
the code's norm over the copy's, per position
deviations: The code is an average over items with S and A held fixed; exp04's copy is item-specific. At the copy dose the code is rescaled to the copy's size, which can be far from its own (both doses are run).
Σ comes from WikiText at the window layers (exp06 estimated 8-40); λ = 0.5 and 0.0 only.
Each window layer is edited on its own, as in exp04.
